CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

scenarios.name: three-accounts
scenarios.why: customer 1 is on file with three accounts of the program's sort code: INQCUST finds it, INQACCCU lists them, DELACC deletes each (ACCOUNT rows gone, a PROCTRAN 'ODA' row each), the CUSTOMER record is read for update and deleted, COMM-DEL-SUCCESS 'Y'

scenarios.name: one-loan
scenarios.why: customer 2, one LOAN account with a negative balance: one DELACC, then the customer is deleted

scenarios.name: no-accounts
scenarios.why: customer 7 is on file with no account: NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS 0, DELETE-ACCOUNTS is not performed, the customer is deleted

scenarios.name: null-statement-date
scenarios.why: customer 3's account has a NULL last-statement date with no indicator: INQACCCU's FETCH fails (-305) and returns no account, so DELCUS deletes the customer alone

scenarios.name: max-values
scenarios.why: customer 6's account holds the extreme picture values (9999.99 rate, 99999999 overdraft, +/-9999999999.99): DELACC's PROCTRAN row and the deletion at the top of every range

scenarios.name: last-customer
scenarios.why: customer 9999999999: INQCUST resolves it to the last customer on file; DELCUS reads and deletes the record keyed 9999999999 (the last one) and its account 99999999

scenarios.name: not-on-file
scenarios.why: customer 5 has an account but no CUSTOMER record: INQCUST fails, COMM-DEL-SUCCESS 'N' with INQCUST's fail code, RETURN; nothing deleted

scenarios.name: customer-zero
scenarios.why: customer 0000000000: INQCUST resolves it to the last customer, the READ of key 0000000000 is NOTFND: the program's own failure path

scenarios.name: read-sysiderr-retried

faults.why: 53 on DELCUS's READ UPDATE (the 3rd READ of CUSTOMER in the task: INQCUST, INQACCCU's INQCUST, DELCUS)

scenarios.why: DELCUS's READ FOR UPDATE gets SYSIDERR once: DELAY 3 seconds (a task takes no time, X4), READ again, then the deletion goes on

scenarios.name: delete-ioerr
scenarios.why: the DELETE of the CUSTOMER record fails with IOERR: the program's failure path

scenarios.name: read-notfnd-after-inquiry

faults.why: 13 on DELCUS's READ UPDATE (the 3rd READ of CUSTOMER in the task: INQCUST, INQACCCU's INQCUST, DELCUS)

scenarios.why: someone else deleted the CUSTOMER record after INQCUST found it: DELCUS's READ FOR UPDATE gets NOTFND and goes to DCV999 -- the accounts are already deleted, the record is not deleted again, COMM-DEL-SUCCESS 'Y'

scenarios.name: read-ioerr

faults.why: 17 on DELCUS's READ UPDATE (the 3rd READ of CUSTOMER in the task)

scenarios.why: DELCUS's READ FOR UPDATE gets IOERR, neither SYSIDERR nor NOTFND: the abend path (ABNDPROC linked, the task abends)

scenarios.name: delete-sysiderr-retried
scenarios.why: the DELETE of the CUSTOMER record gets SYSIDERR once: DELAY 3 seconds (a task takes no time, X4), DELETE again, then the deletion succeeds -- the DELETE twin of read-sysiderr-retried

notes: CBSA's delete-customer service (DELCUS, LINKed by BNK1DCS with the DELCUS copybook's COMMAREA). It LINKs INQCUST (the customer must exist: 'N' and INQCUST's fail code otherwise), lists the customer's accounts through INQACCCU (SYNCONRETURN), LINKs DELACC for each (ACCOUNT row deleted, PROCTRAN 'ODA' row written, as in cbsa-delacc), then READs the CUSTOMER record FOR UPDATE and DELETEs it, retrying on SYSIDERR (DELAY FOR SECONDS(3), no time passes in a task, oracle_assumptions.md X4). ACCOUNT, PROCTRAN, CUSTOMER and ABNDFILE are compared after every scenario. Data: seed.sql is cbsa-delacc's and customer.txt is cbsa-bnk1cca's (SYNTHETIC). Not reached: failure branches no fault can be injected on (ASKTIME / FORMATTIME / ASSIGN, the Db2 INSERT of the PROCTRAN row, LINK DELACC).
